note: Conversations with residents (CITY-007, F-NPC-TALK level 1). The first rule that matches a resident picks their conversation; a resident listed in 'residents' gets that conversation instead (for their own storyline later). A node has the resident's line ('say'), its emotion tag ('mood', used by the faces in CHR-008) and up to 9 replies. A reply has the player's 'text' and 'next': a node id, or null to end the talk. Optional on a reply: 'if', a list of flags that must be set ('name') or not set ('!name'), 'do', flags it sets, and 'act': 'shop' or 'bank' opens that counter where the resident is (ECO-011, BANK-007). Flags are kept per resident; quests will read and set them later. In lines and replies, {name} {role} {place} {doing} {greeting} {weekday} {season} are filled in. Checked by Tools/worldgen/test_world.py.

hello.say: {greeting}! Welcome to {place}. What can I do for you?

menu.say: Anything else I can help with?

today.say: The {season} stock came in this morning. Honestly? Whatever's nearest the window. That's what sells fastest.

options.text: I'll take a look. Anything else?

business.say: Steady. Market days are busy, the rest of the week is regulars. You'd be surprised how many come in just to talk.

options.text: Then I'll leave you to it.

news.say: Someone's been planting flowers round the fountain at night. Nobody's owned up yet.

options.text: Who do you think it is?

news_who.say: No idea! If you find out, tell me first. I've got a bet on with the baker.

flowers.say: Not yet. Ask a gardener. They notice everything that grows.

hello.say: {greeting}. Are you here to be seen, or just visiting?

menu.say: What else can I help with?

symptom.say: Let's see. Tired, hungry, or something worse?

tired.say: Then the cure is a bed, not a pill. Go home, sleep, and come back if it doesn't pass.

hungry.say: There's a café on most corners. Eat something warm and drink some water. Doctor's orders. Well, nurse's.

shift.say: Since six. Mostly small things: scraped knees, and sore backs from the market stalls.

shift2.say: It's good work. People tell you things in here they wouldn't tell anyone else.

hello.say: Oh! Sorry, I can't stop long. I'm {doing}.

busy.say: Same as every {weekday}. The day doesn't run itself!

market.say: Market Square's in the middle of town. Head for the fountain and you can't miss it.

tram.say: Tram Street runs right across the town. Wait at a stop and one comes along soon enough.

hello.say: {greeting}, young one. Stay a while, if you like.

options.text: How long have you lived here?
How long have you lived here?
Tell me more about the old days.

years.say: All my life. Born two streets from here, and I'll likely end up two streets the other way.

options.text: What was it like back then?

before.say: Fewer towers, more gardens. The market was twice the size, and nobody locked a door.

miss.say: Some of it. But the young ones still meet at the fountain at dusk, same as we did. That part never changed.

advice.say: Learn your neighbours' names. Everything else follows from that.

options.text: Just saying hello. I'm new in town.
I'm new in town, by the way.

new.say: Then welcome! I'm {name}. Most people here are friendly, if you give them a minute.

job.say: I'm a {role}. It's not glamorous, but it's mine.

job2.say: Up early, home tired, same as anyone. The good days are the ones where something surprises you.

surprise.say: Ha! Maybe. Don't make it a habit.

weather.say: For {season}? It'll do. Could be worse. Could be raining.
